transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First of all, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening about 1 week after your surgery. However, you should avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for that information. I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you need more of it, your GP should be able to provide some for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful to know! I have another question: I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the clarification. One last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I don't have your specific details, so I'm not sure exactly how long ago your surgery was. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Nope, that's all I have for now. Thanks for the information, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Brilliant! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.

verdict.label: pass

Finally, `escalation_criteria` was covered in turn 8 by advising the patient that "if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further."
